Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid

  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

description: Solve Continual-ARC grid instances by reusing task programs, learning transformations from demos, and validating outputs.

# Continual ARC

Use this procedure for task-id grid puzzles with an available program library.

1. On every instance reply, put exactly one supported action JSON object on the final line. Check `programs/<task id>.py`; when present, run its `transform(grid)` on the test input and submit that exact result before requesting demos. After an incorrect verdict, revise the hypothesis rather than resubmitting the same grid.
2. Parse the grid geometry before inferring a rule: locate every repeated horizontal and vertical divider, including lines interrupted by markers; establish panel bounds, orientation, background, and foreground from positions and examples rather than global color frequency. Identify which intersections or panel features the output encodes.
3. Infer jointly from all demos. Request another only when its possible outcomes distinguish live hypotheses that would change the test answer; weigh the information against demo and attempt costs. A single matching demo does not establish a rule: compare plausible alternatives when ambiguity remains.
4. Implement or repair `transform(grid)`, then execute it on the test and every received demo. Require exact output shape and cell-by-cell agreement with every demo; submit only that program-produced test output. Keep an existing library file intact until the candidate passes all demos; if no candidate is supported, leave it unchanged and continue investigating.
5. A wrong submission is only evidence that the complete rule is wrong; it does not localize the error to particular cells. Revisit all examples and revise the rule, and do not claim verification until all demos agree.
6. After a correct verdict, save the verified transform to `programs/<task id>.py`, replacing the older version, then finish.

Each instance has separate attempt/demo costs. Submission feedback is only correct/incorrect, so use it for hypothesis revision, not cell-level diagnosis.

{
 "path": "/home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-openclawlearner-1792544556/attempts/3223be82bb504fb6b3585b3b468eaac7/system/state/workspace/programs/task-e7230d2b.py",
 "content": "def transform(grid):
    # Copy the populated panel into every panel separated by full divider lines.
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    horizontal = [r for r in range(h) if len(set(grid[r])) == 1 and grid[r][0] != 5]
    vertical = [c for c in range(w) if all(grid[r][c] == grid[0][c] for r in range(h)) and len({grid[r][c] for r in range(h)}) == 1 and grid[0][c] != 5]
    # Identify uniform divider rows/columns by their shared line color.
    div_rows = [r for r in range(h) if len(set(grid[r])) == 1]
    div_cols = [c for c in range(w) if len({grid[r][c] for r in range(h)}) == 1]
    rbounds = [-1] + div_rows + [h]
    cbounds = [-1] + div_cols + [w]
    row_panels = [(rbounds[i]+1, rbounds[i+1]) for i in range(len(rbounds)-1) if rbounds[i+1] > rbounds[i]+1]
    col_panels = [(cbounds[i]+1, cbounds[i+1]) for i in range(len(cbounds)-1) if cbounds[i+1] > cbounds[i]+1]
    # Source panel is the one containing the greatest number of non-background cells.
    panels = [(r0,r1,c0,c1) for r0,r1 in row_panels for c0,c1 in col_panels]
    bg = max(set(x for row in grid for x in row), key=lambda x: sum(v == x for row in grid for v in row))
    src = max(panels, key=lambda p: sum(grid[r][c] != bg for r in range(p[0],p[1]) for c in range(p[2],p[3])))
    pat = [row[src[2]:src[3]] for row in grid[src[0]:src[1]]]
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    for r0,r1 in row_panels:
        for c0,c1 in col_panels:
            for i in range(r1-r0):
                for j in range(c1-c0):
                    out[r0+i][c0+j] = pat[i][j]
    return out
"
